summary:
The Autism Collaboration, Accountability, Research, Education, and Support Act of 2024 (Autism CARES Act of 2024), enacted as Pub. L. 118-180 (H.R. 7213, approved Dec. 23, 2024), amends multiple provisions of the Public Health Service Act (PHSA) to reauthorize and revise federal autism spectrum disorder (ASD) activities through fiscal year 2029.

**NIH Activities (Sec. 2).** Section 2 amends PHSA § 409C (42 U.S.C. 284g). It restructures subsection (a)(1) to direct the Director, in consultation with relevant federal agencies, to conduct basic and clinical research, expanding the enumerated fields (adding psychiatry, psychology, developmental behavioral pediatrics, audiology, and gerontology) and broadening the research scope to co-occurring conditions, caregiver supports, and the full population of ASD individuals across the lifespan. Subsection (b) adds gerontology to Centers of Excellence fields and increases the number of centers from "five" to "seven." Subsection (d) is rewritten to require public-input mechanisms and permit Director guidance on stakeholder engagement. A new subsection (e) directs the Director, for FY 2026–2029, to submit an annual budget estimate to the President for transmittal to Congress (subject to comment but not change by the Secretary and the Interagency Autism Coordinating Committee).

**Programs Relating to Autism (Sec. 3).** Section 3 amends PHSA §§ 399AA–399EE (42 U.S.C. 280i through 280i-4). It revises the surveillance and research program (§ 399AA), education/early-detection/intervention provisions (§ 399BB)—substituting "culturally and linguistically appropriate" for "culturally competent," "at increased likelihood" for "at higher risk," and reworking the intervention grant/contract authority under subsection (f)—and the Interagency Autism Coordinating Committee (§ 399CC), consolidating its strategic-plan duties and requiring annual and biennial updates to Congress and the President. It extends multiple sunset dates from "December 20, 2024" to "September 30, 2029" (§§ 399AA(e), 399BB(g), 399CC(f)).

Section 3(b)(10) requires a report within 2 years on developmental-behavioral pediatrician training. Section 3(d) amends § 399DD reporting requirements (updating "2019" references to "2024"), refocuses subsection (b) from "health and well-being" to "mental health needs," and adds a subsection (c) requiring, within 2 years, an update on youth transitioning to adulthood.

Section 3(e) amends the authorization of appropriations under § 399EE for FY 2025–2029: increasing subsection (a) from $23,100,000 to $28,100,000; subsection (b) from $50,599,000 to $56,344,000; and subsection (c) from $296,000,000 to $306,000,000 per fiscal year. These are authorizations, not appropriations.

**Technical Assistance (Sec. 4).** Section 4 (codified as a note to 42 U.S.C. 280i) grants discretionary authority to the Secretary to provide, upon jurisdictional request, training and technical assistance regarding federal funding for communication-supporting services and technologies, and requires an annual report to the specified committees.
